content.title: USMNT's problems resurface in 2-0 friendly defeat to Portugal — 'It's just the same story'
content.text: ATLANTA — Mauricio Pochettino and the U.S. national soccer team were, by no means, in desperate need of victory Tuesday. It was, after all, another friendly against a top-10 opponent on the ever-shortening road to the World Cup.But what Pochettino needed to see was unmistakable improvement after a weekend fiasco. He needed to see greater intensity and concentration, fewer defensive errors and a killer instinct in front of the goal.AdvertisementMany of the telltale signs of a team unprepared to make a deep run this summer surfaced again, however, resulting in a 2-0 loss to Portugal before an announced crowd of 72,297 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.Draft your Yahoo Fantasy Baseball team for the 2026 MLB SeasonThe next time Pochettino gathers his squad will be late May for the World Cup roster announcement in New York, followed by two more friendlies and then the Group D opener June 12 against Paraguay in the Los Angeles area.AdvertisementDespite the setbacks, Pochettino and the players exuded confidence that they will turn things around in time for the tournament.“We are so close to the World Cup, but I think we are intelligent enough to know what we need to do,” Pochettino said. “I am more positive now than before, because seeing the team compete, we are not far away. It's only details that we need to improve. When we match the opponent in the areas that we need to match, we are going to have the possibility to beat them.”Maybe the Americans will find their way in pre-tournament camp and final tuneups to make a run in the summer spectacle, to be staged in 16 cities across North America. But as things stand, they will have enough trouble just getting through a balanced quartet in the first stage.AdvertisementLike Saturday, when they were humbled here by Belgium 5-2, the Americans played well in the first half against a superior foe. But nothing came of their attacking work, most notably from star Christian Pulisic, whose scoring slump — and frustration — grew.Portugal was quite the opposite, striking with pinpoint efficiency eight minutes before intermission and taking advantage of the U.S.’ stunning inattention on a second-half corner kick.“In details, in small details, I think we lose the game,” Pochettino said.AdvertisementMalik Tillman of United States reacts after the first goal of Portugal scored by Francisco Trincao of Portugal (not in frame) during the international friendly match between United States and Portugal at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on March 31, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Kevin C. Cox via Getty Images)The two defeats came after an uplifting end to 2025: four victories and a draw against World Cup-bound teams. With momentum halted, the U.S. will aim to regain its rhythm in friendlies against Senegal on May 31 in Charlotte and Germany on June 6 in Chicago.“We caused the teams a lot of problems,” Pulisic said. “We put a lot of pressure on them. We did a lot of great things. … It's just the same story, but I feel we’re really close and I feel like we're in a good place, so I'm going to stay positive.”AdvertisementReturning to the lineup after sitting out Saturday, goalkeeper Matt Freese made multiple excellent saves and wasn’t at fault on the goals, which were the result of defensive shortcomings.“I do think there are pockets of positives and pockets of play in areas where it worked great,” he said. “There are little details that can take us to the next level, and it's important we continue to work on them — and work on them quickly.”Pochettino made five other lineup changes, inserting defenders Chris Richards, Auston Trusty and Alex Freeman, and midfielders Sebastian Berhalter and Aidan Morris.AdvertisementStriker Folarin Balogun’s lineup absence was not a surprise. (In two-game friendly windows, Pochettino typically splits starting assignments.) What was a surprise was the absence of a straight-up replacement, Ricardo Pepi or Patrick Agyemang.Without a pure striker, Pulisic played up front. He received central support from Malik Tillman and Weston McKennie, while Tim Weah and Antonee Robinson buzzed the flanks.Pochettino on Monday spoke about the need to get Pulisic in better positions to score and break out of his 12-game scoring rut for AC Milan. His last national team goal came in November 2024, although, because of injuries and rest, he missed multiple camps last year.AdvertisementOn Tuesday, Pulisic was off target again, collected a yellow card and departed at halftime.“He feels frustrated, and that is what we want, what we expect. He was fighting, he was committed in the phases that we demand more,” Pochettino said. “I am sure he is going to come back to his club and he's going to start to score again.”Pulisic said, “I know I'm going to get to the other side, and things are going to click.”Coached by Spaniard Roberto Martinez, Portugal arrived in Atlanta following a 0-0 draw with Mexico on Saturday at renovated Estadio Azteca. Aside from injured superstar Cristiano Ronaldo, the roster excluded Manchester City’s injured pair, defender Ruben Dias and midfielder Bernardo Silva.AdvertisementStill, Martinez set an impressive lineup, featuring Manchester United’s Bruno Fernandes and Paris Saint-Germain’s Vitinha and Gonçalo Ramos. Only three players started both matches.At the start, the Americans crackled with energy and purpose, just as they had done Saturday. Again, though, they failed to capitalize. Pulisic’s first opportunity came in the sixth minute on an overlap with Tillman, but his angled bid targeting the far side was blocked by a defender.Freese was tested two minutes later, getting down quickly to touch aside Fernandes’ effort streaking to the far corner.AdvertisementThe U.S. showed the ability to alleviate pressure and launch forays. There was no payoff, however.Portugal scored a minute after a Pulisic miss — a repeat of Saturday, when Pulisic squandered a golden opportunity and Belgium quickly responded with the go-ahead goal.On this night, the attempt came from much greater distance, but again was off target, zipping past the left post by a whisker.In the 37th minute, Vitinha’s through ball to Fernandes unlocked the U.S. defense. Without a proper shooting angle, Fernandes back-heeled the ball to unmarked Francisco Trincao for a 10-yarder into the far corner.AdvertisementPulisic’s frustration mounted. At the end of an aborted run into the box, he intentionally kicked Samu Costa and received a yellow card. Pulisic had been warned earlier for a late challenge on Vitinha.The lead doubled in the 59th minute. As Fernandes prepared to serve a corner kick, no one marked substitute João Félix at the top of the box — eight U.S. players were in or near the 6-yard box and two others stood between the corner and the net.Fernandes identified his open teammate. With an abundance of time and space, Félix cooly settled the ball before lashing a half-volley through a crowd and into the lower left corner.Advertisement“It's hard to say we're where we want to be with results like this, but we take a lot of positives from the games, and we see that we can keep up,” McKennie said. “We were definitely toe to toe, and we just can't let things slip away.”Pochettino ended up making nine changes in the second half. None made a lasting impact. The U.S.’s empty camp was over, leaving the beleaguered coach with precious little time to solve the problems ahead of the World Cup.AdvertisementHere’s how Tuesday’s match unfolded in real-time:Live coverage has finished19 updatesWed 1 April 2026 at 1:06 am UTCThe USMNT is held scoreless as Portugal nets two goals in the final game before Mauricio Pochettino names his World Cup roster in May. He also left open the possibility of remaining with the U.S. after his program-record $6 million a year contract expires after the World Cup.“I think everyone knows I am committed [to] the national team here” for the World Cup, the Argentine said. There is “no point to talk about the future at the moment, but no one approached. Who knows what is going to happen? We are open. We don't have a [U.S.] contract for the future. But why not, if we are happy and the [U.S. Soccer] Federation is happy? It’s about [finding out].
